historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle revenue growth. revenue_5yr_cagr (6.5%) haircut for the FY2026 contraction and the permitting bottleneck on community count; equity CAGR is distorted by buybacks exceeding earnings and EPS CAGR by the shrinking share count, so neither is a usable growth anchor for NVR.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 4.5% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 13.7% and revenue 6.5%: >30% divergence. NVR retires nearly all earnings via buybacks (FY2024 buybacks $2,058M vs net income $1,682M), so book value barely grows while per-share EPS compounds; the equity CAGR is a capital-allocation artefact, not a growth signal.
historical_growth.notes: Unchanged from the 2026-10-02 build: FY0 is still FY2025, so the annual CAGRs have no new endpoint. Owner-FCF CAGRs are computed on the SBC- and interest-income-adjusted series. 3-year CAGRs (-0.65% revenue, -18.7% owner FCF) run from the FY2022 house-price peak (21.6% EBITDA margin) to FY2025 (16.6%) and describe the down-leg of a cycle, not a trend. The owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-18.7%) is worse than the reported (-16.0%) mainly because interest income on the 2023-24 cash pile was flattering reported FCF; that stream is now shrinking with the cash.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 revenue -12.5% at a 13.5% EBITDA margin on nine months of actuals; a 13.0% trough in FY2027 as gross margin keeps sliding, then 4-5% growth as rates ease and the lot pipeline converts, and a 14.5% mid-cycle margin -- below the 2021-24 house-price-inflation years, above the pre-2017 range.
scenario_narratives.bull: Mortgage rates reverse to the high-5s during 2027 and permitting relief unlocks the 176k controlled lots; entry-level shortage drives 8% growth in FY2028-29 and margins recapture 16.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Rates keep rising and spec-builder discounting takes share from build-to-order NVR; two down years, 11% trough margin recovering only to 12%; earnings-power case, not solvency.

valuation_philosophy.summary: NVR is valued as an operating cyclical on owner FCF: SBC expensed, interest income on the (now much smaller) cash pile stripped and the net cash added once, the share count held flat, and cyclicality handled by normalising the EBITDA margin from the FY2026-27 trough across three explicit paths rather than by a WACC premium. The capital-light lot-option model makes owner FCF track net income closely (capex and D&A are ~0.3% of revenue), so the valuation is essentially a question of what mid-cycle margin and growth the market should capitalise, and at what rate -- and the market price sits above the base case, between the base and bull margin paths.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: the rebuild on a 5.07% 10y yield (WACC 10.25%, was 9.5%) is the largest single change in this update, worth about -9% of value; each 0.5pp of WACC is roughly 6-7% of base value. If the 10y falls back toward 4.5% the rate, and the value, move back.
Mid-cycle margin judgment: each 1pp of mature EBITDA margin is worth roughly 7-8% of base value; the 14.5% base sits between the 12.9% pre-2017 average and the 16.9% post-2017 average.
Mortgage-rate path drives both volume and price; the scenarios span a reversal to the high-5s to a further rise, but a 2008-style credit event is outside all three.

Community-count bottleneck: controlled lots are up 68% since 2019 but active communities are roughly flat, and lots fell to 176,000 in Q3 2026 from 184,400 as NVR walked from deposits; if permitting does not clear, the FY2028-30 growth in base does not arrive.
Lot-deposit impairments scale with price declines ($55.4M in 9M 2026, $24.8M in Q3; 24,000 controlled lots carry a $156M allowance); a sharper price reset would add to the bear case.

Flat share count understates the per-share compounding NVR has delivered historically; buybacks executed below intrinsic value add value the model does not credit (and above it, destroy value it does not debit).

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement add-back (XBRL us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation, $69,213k). No PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation tag exists for NVR -- awards are mostly options settled by cash exercise (proceeds $80.1M FY2025), so there is no net-share-settlement withholding to add; SBC incl. equity taxes equals the add-back. 9M 2026 add-back $55.4M (Q3 2026 10-Q), 0.84% of 9M revenue.
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 2,645,788 cover-page shares at 2026-10-31 (Q3 2026 10-Q) + 120,265 dilutive option/RSU increment from the Q3 2026 EPS table = 2,766,053. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count. NVR is a heavy repurchaser ($1,833M FY2025, $1,243M 9M 2026 per the cash flow statement; $823M of authorisation left at 2026-09-30; count down from 6.1M in 2010 to 2.65M), so the flat count is more than funded; buybacks beyond the SBC offset are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: risk-free 5.07% (10y UST, ^TNX close 2026-11-18; it has held 4.9-5.3% since mid-September), ERP 5.0%, equity beta ~1.1 (NVR's 5y beta vs S&P sits 1.0-1.2; below spec-building, land-owning peers) -> cost of equity ~10.6%; the $900M of 3.0% senior notes due 2030 are ~5.5% of capital at ~4.5% after tax, giving WACC ~10.25%. CORRECTION to the 2026-10-02 build, which stated a ~4.1% 10y UST and 9.5%: the 10y was in fact ~5.2-5.3% on that date, so the prior rate was built on a stale risk-free. Housing cyclicality and rate sensitivity are charged ONCE, in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight -- not stacked into WACC, and WACC is identical across the three scenarios (owner-fcf-adaptations (f)).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating-lease cost (offices, model homes) is already an operating expense inside EBITDA/EBIT, so no separate lease line is charged and lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. One treatment, consistently applied. Finance leases are immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- NVR has no non-controlling interests.
inputs.interest_income_treatment: EBITDA in core_metrics was derived as pretax income + homebuilding interest expense - homebuilding other income (which is almost entirely interest on the cash pile) + D&A, so the forward flows exclude interest income by construction, and FY2025 interest income of $96.3M is stripped from the owner-FCF anchor. Net cash ($217.7M at 2026-09-30: homebuilding cash 1,091.3 + mortgage-banking cash 34.1 less senior notes 907.7; restricted cash excluded) is added once in the bridge. Net cash is well below 1x the FCF base because ~$3.1B of buybacks since end-FY2024 ran down the pile -- corporate interest income fell to $38.3M in 9M 2026 from $65.1M -- which is exactly why the FY2025 interest income must not be carried forward.
inputs.mortgage_banking_note: NVR Mortgage Finance funds loans held for sale with a repurchase facility secured by those loans (undrawn at 2026-09-30); it is excluded from total_debt (senior notes only, consistent with the Metrics CSV) and treated as working capital of the segment. Mortgage banking pretax (~3% of revenue, ~10% of 9M 2026 pretax as homebuilding profit fell) is inside the consolidated EBITDA margin.
inputs.timing_note: Year 1 is FY2026 (Dec year-end), with nine months reported and most of Q4 elapsed at the valuation date, while the balance sheet is at 2026-09-30. 9M 2026 owner FCF (~$290M after SBC and corporate interest income, ~$105/share) has already been spent on buybacks and so sits in the lower share count as well as in the year-1 flow. Against that, the engine's end-of-year convention discounts every later flow roughly 0.9 of a year too long (FY2027 arrives ~1.1 years out, not 2). The second effect is the larger, so the convention is mildly conservative on net; it is the folder standard and is left as is.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (owner-fcf.md + the cyclical adaptations), 10-year explicit horizon because margins are being normalised from a FY2026-27 trough, not carried forward. NVR is a US homebuilder -- an operating cyclical with no banking, REIT or holdco features -- so the routing table sends it to the owner-FCF engine; the mid-cycle treatment lives in the margin paths (FY2026 ~13.5% EBITDA margin recovering to 14.5% base / 16.5% bull / 12% bear) rather than in a mid-cycle FCF override. UPDATE of the 2026-10-02 valuation, same model: anchors refreshed to the Q3 2026 10-Q, FY2026 drivers re-judged on nine months of actuals, FY2027 margin trimmed, WACC rebuilt on the actual 10y yield; everything else deliberately unchanged (see reconciliation.unchanged). Reported FCF for FY2025 is OCF $1,121.3M less capex $24.5M = $1,096.8M; owner FCF = 1,096.8 - 69.2 SBC - 96.3 interest income = $931.3M (9.0% of revenue). Working-capital caveat: the -10% capture releases ~$129M in FY2026 on the modelled revenue decline, whereas 9M 2026 actually consumed cash (inventory under sales agreements +$531M with the backlog build, partly offset by a $254M fall in mortgage loans held for sale); most of that inventory settles in Q4, but year-1 FCF may be overstated by up to ~$50/share.

bear.narrative: Q4 2026 backlog turnover slips again and cancellations (21% in Q3) stay elevated (FY2026 -13.5%, 13.3% margin). Rates keep rising into 2027 and a labour-market downturn follows; spec-heavy national builders (DHI, LEN, PHM) discount finished inventory that build-to-order NVR cannot match, so volume and price both give way (FY2027 -8%). Further lot-deposit impairments follow the $55.4M of 9M 2026, and NVR keeps walking from lots as it did in Q3. Margins trough at 11% -- the FY2013-16 range -- and recover only to 12% as community count stays bottlenecked. No solvency question: net cash, no land book, 3% notes due 2030; the bear is an earnings-power case, not a survival case.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 -12.5% (was -8%): 9M 2026 revenue $6,610M is -13.2% YoY, and the H2 recovery the October build assumed did not arrive -- Q3 settlements were -7% in units at -2% price because backlog turnover fell (48% of opening backlog settled vs 56% a year earlier; management cites labour capacity). Q4 enters with backlog of 10,121 units / $4,585M (+10% units, +4% dollars), which at ~52% turnover and a ~$447k settlement price gives ~$2.4B, about -10% YoY. FY2027 flat on that lower base, UNCHANGED as a rate: the year-end backlog should still be up mid-single digits in dollars, offsetting Q3 new orders of -7% units and -5% price. FY2028-30 4-5% as rates ease and the 176,000 controlled lots (+68% since 2019) convert to communities as permitting clears; fading to 2.5% nominal (household formation + inflation) by year 10 -- all UNCHANGED.
base.margin_rationale: EBITDA margin (ex interest income) was 10.7-12.5% in FY2013-16, 13.8-14.9% in FY2017-20, 18.5-21.6% at the FY2021-22 house-price peak, 19.2% FY2023-24 and 16.6% FY2025. 9M 2026 ran 13.5% (H1 13.2%, Q3 14.0% on seasonal SG&A leverage; homebuilding gross margin 19.0% for 9M and 18.3% in Q3 vs 21.1%, with $55.4M of lot-deposit impairments year to date). FY2026 base is therefore 13.5% (was 14.0%). FY2027 trough cut to 13.0% (was 13.5%): gross margin was still falling in Q3, new-order prices sit below settlement prices, and the 10-Q expects further margin pressure from higher land prices and community repositioning. Recovery to 14.0% in FY2028 and a 14.5% mid-cycle from FY2029 is UNCHANGED: the FY2017-25 average ex the two peak years, and above the pre-2017 range because scale and the land-light model have improved structurally.
base.sbc_rationale: SBC was 0.67% of revenue FY2025 and 0.84% in 9M 2026 (fixed-dollar option grants over a smaller revenue base): 0.82% for FY2026, 0.80% FY2027, then the prior 0.75% as revenue recovers -- it is a rounding line for NVR.
base.capex_da_rationale: NVR owns almost no land or plant: D&A 0.24% and capex 0.24% of FY2025 revenue (24.5M each). 9M 2026 capex was $29.9M (Q3 alone $18.9M) and D&A $19.8M, so FY2026 is set at 0.42% / 0.30%; the Q3 spike is treated as one year's production-facility spend and later years keep the prior 0.28% / 0.25%.
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 cash taxes $438.8M on ~$1,762M pretax = 24.9%; GAAP provision 24.0%; 9M 2026 provision 24.5%. 24.5% held flat -- no NOLs, no valuation-allowance noise, federal 21% + state. UNCHANGED.
base.wc_rationale: Negative capture: growth consumes cash through lot deposits and homes under construction (OCF ran $220-310M below net income in FY2024-25 as controlled lots grew). -10% of the revenue change is below the recent 2-3%-of-revenue consumption because that included a deliberate counter-cyclical lot-pipeline build, which has now stopped (controlled lots fell in Q3 2026). UNCHANGED; see the working-capital caveat in inputs.notes for FY2026.
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 15x owner FCF (cyclical range 12-15x; NVR has earned the top of it with 40%+ ROE and net cash). Gordon at 10.25%/2.5% = 13.2x, so Gordon binds and the cap is a brake only.
base.narrative: Demand weakened further in Q3 2026 and mortgage rates rose; FY2026 revenue falls 12.5% and margins trough at 13% in FY2027. Rates then grind down, affordability repairs slowly, NVR holds share with its build-to-order model, community count catches up to the lot pipeline, and margins settle at a 14.5% mid-cycle well below the 2021-24 house-price-inflation peak.

bull.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 10.25%/3.0% = 14.2x now binds; at the prior 9.5% the 15x cap bound.
bull.narrative: Q4 2026 backlog turnover recovers (FY2026 -11.5%, 13.8% margin). Mortgage rates reverse their 2026 rise and fall to the high-5s during 2027, the ~500k-unit shortfall of sub-$260k homes pulls Ryan Homes entry-level demand forward, permitting clears so the 176k controlled lots convert to community-count growth, and the land-light model recaptures a 16.5% EBITDA margin -- the FY2017-25 average including the peak years, still short of FY2023-24's 19%. FY2027 margin starts lower than previously modelled (14.5%, was 15.0%) because gross margin was still falling in Q3 2026. Revenue compounds 8% through FY2028-29 and the buyback keeps shrinking the count.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25, UNCHANGED from the 2026-10-02 build (moved then from the 15/50/35 house default). Bear at 25%: homebuilding is a rate-driven cyclical in a down-leg that Q3 2026 extended (demand weakened further, new orders -7%, cancellations 21%, mortgage rates rising), and a labour-market turn would extend it again -- though the bear is an earnings case with no balance-sheet risk, which is why it is not higher. The Q3 deterioration is already carried in the re-anchored FY2026-27 drivers of all three scenarios, so it is not also charged through the weights. Bull at 25%: it needs three independent things -- rates reversing to the high-5s, municipal permitting clearing so community count catches the lot pipeline, and margins recapturing 16.5% without the house-price inflation that produced the 2021-24 margins.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
